topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the learning objectives for the final lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional therapeutic modalities, focusing on surgical resection, radiotherapy, and systemic cytotoxic chemotherapy along with their mechanisms and side effects.

topics.label: Exploiting cellular vulnerabilities and genetic defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss therapeutic strategies designed to exploit specific vulnerabilities and genetic abnormalities of cancer cells, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and defective DNA repair.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on treating oncogene-addicted cancers with small-molecule kinase inhibitors while detailing the molecular mechanisms of drug resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapies and conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the use of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates to direct cytotoxic effects against tumor-associated surface antigens.

topics.label: Tumor immunology and cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of cancer immune surveillance and the development of immunotherapies that reactivate or engineer T-cell responses against tumors.

topics.label: Progress, ongoing challenges, and future perspectives in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the clinical challenges, historical survival trends, genomic stratification methods, and ethical considerations shaping modern and future cancer management.
